requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present and the edge cases are handled: queues migration has cascade FK + `unique(['entity_id','slug'])` + `is_active` default true (database/migrations/2026_10_29_080615_create_queues_table.php:8-17); tickets migration has `cascadeOnDelete`, unique `['queue_id','code']`, the recommended `['queue_id','status','priority','issued_at']` index and nullable `called_by_user_id` (database/migrations/2026_10_29_080616_create_tickets_table.php:16-30); `nextCode()` scans by `orderByDesc('id')` and skips malformed codes (app/Models/Ticket.php:94-110); the action locks and re-reads the queue inside the transaction and rejects inactive queues (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:42-49), rejects negative priority before any write (:36), and retries 5 times on a code collision (:40, :61); write-once guard (app/Models/Ticket.php:64-75) and single-call with `lockForUpdate` + membership check (app/Models/Ticket.php:119-146); factory allocates the code in `afterMaking` and preserves explicit codes, plus `forQueue()` (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:34-45); Queue casts/relations and `Entity::queues()` (app/Models/Queue.php:34-46, app/Models/Entity.php:45-48); both docs and CHANGELOG updated.

conventions.evidence: Domain write is an invokable action with no constructor (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:31-54), migrations are reversible and match generator stubs (`down()` in both migration files), docs/CHANGELOG kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md '### Issuance', docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md:9), PHPDoc on public methods. Deviation: authorization is an inline `$user->membershipFor($entityId)` check rather than a policy/gate as required by conventions.md ('Authorization always goes through policies/gates') (app/Models/Ticket.php:135). Model fillable uses the class-level `#[Fillable]` attribute rather than the `$fillable` property used elsewhere (app/Models/Queue.php:12, app/Models/Ticket.php:16).

security.evidence: No weakness found. Every action authorizes server-side: `call()` resolves the locked row, derives the entity from the queue and rejects non-members with `AuthorizationException` before writing (app/Models/Ticket.php:127-141). Status is re-checked after locking so a stale waiting model cannot double-call (:127-132). Inputs are typed (`int $priority`, `TicketChannel`) and negative priority is rejected (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:36, :49-53); queries are bound Eloquent, no raw SQL and no output rendering. `#[Fillable]` lists exactly the persisted fields (app/Models/Ticket.php:16-25) and the write-once guard blocks later mutation of all but the call fields (:64-75).

tests.evidence: Six Pest files cover the requirements and the failure paths: issuance defaults, consecutive codes, negative priority, inactive queue and stale model, DI resolution, collision retry (tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php:13-107); factory code allocation/insertion order/malformed codes/deletion/queue scoping (tests/Feature/Queue/TicketFactoryTest.php:10-83); schema, defaults, unique indexes and cascades (tests/Feature/Queue/TicketSchemaTest.php:10-81); model casts and relations (tests/Feature/Queue/QueueTicketTest.php:10-78); happy path, all roles, non-member, other-entity member, already-called and double-call, plus immutability through save and update (tests/Feature/Queue/TicketCallTest.php:23-158). No existing test is weakened or deleted.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: one action, one small guard, no extra layers. Two avoidable costs: `nextCode()` plucks every code of the queue and scans them in PHP (app/Models/Ticket.php:98-104), which grows with queue size; collision detection hand-rolls SQLSTATE/message matching (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:72-77) where Laravel's `UniqueConstraintViolationException` already exists. The duplicated `TicketStatus::Waiting` check in `call()` (:121 and :131) is deliberate re-validation after locking and is fine.

readability.evidence: Short focused methods, intention-revealing names (`nextCode`, `isCodeCollision`, `calledBy`), useful docblocks that explain why (app/Models/Ticket.php:88-93, :113-118; app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:34-48), no dead code, no debug output and consistent formatting throughout the diff.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: the two migrations, models/enums/exception/action/factories, the `Entity::queues()` addition, the six test files and the directly related docs (business-rules, database-schema, architecture link, docs/README, CHANGELOG). No unrelated refactors or extra features; `TicketFactory::forQueue()`/`QueueFactory::inactive()` are required or used by the tests.

issues.explanation: Ticket calling authorizes with an inline `$user->membershipFor($entityId)` check, whereas conventions require authorization to go through a policy/gate in `app/Policies/` (a `TicketPolicy`/gate would also give the authorization a single, testable home).

Code-collision detection matches SQLSTATE '23000' plus the words 'unique'/'duplicate' in the driver message; catching `Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException` is driver-agnostic and removes the string heuristics.
`nextCode()` loads every code of the queue into memory and scans them on each issuance; a backwards query/chunked walk would keep cost bounded as a queue grows.

The class-level `#[Fillable]` attribute differs from the `$fillable` property used by sibling models; confirm the attribute ships in the pinned Laravel version (composer.json is not available here) so mass assignment is actually configured.

The test registers a static `Ticket::creating` listener that is never removed, so it stays active for the rest of the PHP process; it is harmless after its guard flag flips, but `Ticket::flushEventListeners()` (or clearing the listener) in a cleanup would keep tests isolated.
The single-call lock is only exercised sequentially; there is no test for two concurrent callers, and no test for `called_by_user_id` being nulled when the calling user is deleted.

review.summary: This change adds the queue/ticket persistence and domain core exactly as specified: generated-style migrations with the required cascade/uniques/index, Queue/Ticket models with enums and a write-once guard, a transactional IssueTicket action that re-reads and locks the queue, per-queue display-code allocation that skips legacy codes, and a single-call `Ticket::call()` with membership authorization. It is well tested (including failure, authorization and code edge cases) and docs/CHANGELOG are in sync. The remaining concerns are a conventions deviation (inline membership check instead of a policy/gate), fragile collision detection via SQLSTATE/message matching, an unbounded `nextCode()` scan, and a few nits, so it is approvable after minor cleanup.
